title: PPIA-15 Deterministic Oracle, Fixture Isolation and Evidence Rules

oracle_model.rule: The oracle describes externally and authoritatively governed results, not an implementation technique. When source authority does not define an outcome, the deterministic expected result is explicit unsupported/indeterminate behavior rather than a guessed rule.

authority_rules: Permission and entitlement resolution precede protected object resolution, counts, search, selection, actions, diagnostics, support, export, notifications and optional AI context.
When existence is protected, hidden and missing must remain externally equivalent across wording, counts, timing, action availability and recovery behavior.
Local draft/edit state, save intent, authoritative command, accepted durable Event and derived projection/cache are distinct phases.
status-unknown is not failure and must not authorize blind mutation retry.
An accepted durable Event with projection lag is not an unsuccessful command.
Offline/local state is not authoritative mutation.
Every owning-domain mutation contract retains its expected-version, operation-id, authorization and idempotency semantics; PPIA-15 does not create a new mutation protocol.
AI may consume only the authorized redacted projection and cannot decide permission, approval, recovery, canonical truth, balance or promotion.
conflict_and_concurrency_rules: Silent last-write-wins is forbidden for governed conflicts.

Two concurrent intents must either resolve through the owning-domain contract to one accepted authoritative outcome, reject one or both with explicit conflict/current-version state, or remain status-unknown pending lookup.
Compatible duplicate operation IDs converge to the prior result/status; incompatible operation-ID reuse fails without mutation where the owning domain specifies idempotency.
A new PPIA-15 case cannot assert merge semantics that the owning domain has not defined.
scale_rules: Every scale/density case declares a concrete synthetic fixture count inside that case.
Case-local counts are QA stress inputs only and never establish supported maximums, performance budgets or release guarantees.
Scale tests must preserve stable identity, deterministic ordering/filtering where specified, permission-safe aggregates and semantic accessibility.

PPIA-11 analysis may surface low/moderate/high/indeterminate uncertainty and may terminate indeterminate_blocked when governing interaction rules are missing; no balanced/fair/safe/winnable/optimal/guaranteed oracle is permitted.

provenance_classes.meaning: Exact existing fixture/case or one-to-one execution representation; additive count zero when aliased.
Existing cases/contracts used as component proofs for a new cross-domain or timing composition.
New PPIA-15 deterministic QA case adding a material test dimension; noncanonical.
Case intentionally proves unsupported/indeterminate behavior because upstream authority is missing.
Future execution evidence from a candidate build; evidence only, not source truth or automatic canon.

evidence_requirements: Every future executed scenario records exact candidate/build identity, fixture version/digest, role/authority state, operation IDs when applicable, expected oracle and actual result.
Execution evidence is separate from the design-time scenario definition and cannot retroactively change its source basis.
A passing scenario proves only the bounded case; it does not imply complete-game coverage, production readiness, tester authorization or release approval.
A failing scenario remains unfinished evidence and cannot be converted to pass through wording alone.
